learningObjective: Explain the role of a Device Mesh as a logical named-axis grid decoupled from the physical topology.
stem: In GSPMD / XLA-style SPMD, a job runs on 32 GPUs organized as a Device Mesh of shape [8, 4] with named axes ('data', 'model'). Which statement about the Mesh abstraction is correct?

options.text: The Device Mesh is a logical grid: sharding specs reference axis names, and the runtime is free to map mesh coordinates to physical devices in different ways (e.g. to align an axis with fast NVLink links).
Once axes are named 'data' and 'model', the compiler forbids sharding any tensor along the 'model' axis if it is also sharded along the 'data' axis; sharding must be exclusive to a single mesh axis.
The Device Mesh is a physical topology descriptor: axes must be named to match the underlying NVLink/PCIe layout, and changing axis assignments requires physically recabling the cluster.
The Mesh is a NCCL runtime object; the compiler IR does not represent it, so all mesh-related decisions happen at runtime and cannot influence which collectives are inserted.

explanation: The Device Mesh is a logical named-axis abstraction. Sharding specs reference axis names (e.g. sharding a weight along 'model'); the runtime chooses how to map mesh coordinates to physical devices, typically to align high-bandwidth axes (like 'model' which sees frequent AllReduces) with fast intra-node links. A is a physical-topology confusion. B is wrong: a tensor can be sharded along multiple axes simultaneously (e.g. sharded on both 'data' and 'model'). D is wrong: the mesh is a compile-time IR concept that drives partitioning.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: mesh is logical; physical mapping is separate.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: multi-axis sharding is common and supported.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: mesh axes do not represent physical wiring.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the mesh is represented at the IR / compile-time level.

assumptions: Sharding specs reference mesh axes by name.
nonImplications: Does not imply that any mapping performs equally well; aligning collectives with fast links matters.
Does not imply that mesh shape can be changed mid-execution.

distractorRationales.D: Ignores the compiler-level role of the mesh.
